To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) bias correction of directional variables requires a circular‐circular transformation, and (2) a Bayesian model averaging technique for directional variables can be used to calibrate directional ensemble forecasts, where the ensemble members are individually bias corrected.

(i) bias correction and Bayesian model averaging are effective methods for improving the quality of surface wind direction forecasts, (ii) the bias correction method is based on a novel circular‐circular linear regression approach, and (iii) Bayesian model averaging is implemented using a von Mises mixture model, which is a generalization of the traditional von Mises model.

(a) a circular-circular regression method for bias correction is developed and applied to wind direction forecasts; (b) a Bayesian model averaging technique for directional variables is proposed, where the component densities are von Mises distributions; (c) the proposed methods yield significant improvements in forecast performance, and (d) the methods are applicable to a broad range of meteorological variables.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new approach for the postprocessing of ensemble forecasts of surface wind directions.
the development and application of new techniques to improve the quality of ensemble forecasts of wind direction, which can be used in a wide range of operational settings.
the development and evaluation of statistical postprocessing methods for ensemble forecasts of wind direction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed methods for bias correction and ensemble calibration are very effective for directional variables and should be considered for application in other areas where wind direction is an important variable.
our new bias correction technique is effective for directional variables, and the Bayesian model averaging approach is effective for ensemble forecasts of directional variables.
the proposed bias correction and Bayesian model averaging techniques for wind direction forecasts are very effective, and should be applied to any operational ensemble forecasting system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed and implemented an effective bias correction and Bayesian model averaging technique for ensemble forecasts of surface wind directions.

the circular regression and Bayesian model averaging approaches are effective for correcting and calibrating directional forecasts from numerical weather models, which are essential components for the development of probabilistic wind energy forecasts.
the bias correction method and the Bayesian model averaging scheme are both effective for wind direction ensemble forecasts.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the proposed bias correction and ensemble postprocessing techniques are generally applicable, and can be used for any directional variable, including, e.g., the wind direction of tropical cyclones, or the direction of ocean currents.
the bias‐corrected ensemble forecasts are superior to the original ensemble forecasts, even if the original forecasts are not biased.
the bias-correction and postprocessing methods for wind direction forecasts can be based on the same circular‐circular statistical techniques as for wind direction observations.
